extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark designed to systematically evaluate multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6,092 QA pairs across diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data combines large-scale real-world robotic datasets (e.g., Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RoboMIND, AgiBot World Colosseo, RDT-1B) with curated in-house collection. It extracts frame sequences from robotic videos across single-arm, dual-arm, mobile-manipulator, and humanoid robot embodiments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: High-quality robotic manipulation and navigation videos and open-source datasets including RH20T, Open X-Embodiment, RoboMIND, AgiBot World Colosseo, RDT-1B, as well as in-house robotic collection.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For instruction comprehension, explicit instructions were rewritten into demand-based implicit requests using LLMs. For planning tasks, natural language steps were converted to predefined function sequences and instantiated with arguments. Planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage quality control process was implemented: filtering during construction (applying general criteria for image quality/task validity and task-specific filters like excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks) and post-construction validation. Items that all models solve correctly were removed via a majority-vote strategy, while items that all models fail to solve underwent manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were performed via a hybrid workflow involving multimodal foundation models (Gemini) and human experts. Gemini generated structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata), which were refined by human annotators. In perception, static attributes were combined with GPT-generated functional properties, Gemini-segmented video steps, and manual annotations of relative positions, keypoints, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Affordance annotations (static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, mobile base positions) were labeled on sampled representative frames. Execution-level failures from RoboMIND were labeled by experts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Post-construction validation was conducted using a majority-vote strategy across model evaluations: items solved correctly by all models were removed to ensure difficulty, and items that all models failed to solve were manually reviewed and corrected. 20 professionally trained annotators inspected linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators and domain experts.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (Comanici et al., 2025), GPT models, and detection models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models evaluated show significant performance drops on implicit instructions, struggle with robotic-view recognition, spatiotemporal reasoning, cross-scenario planning (such as dual-arm coordination and rare-object reasoning), fine-grained affordance understanding, and execution-level failure diagnosis.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation and planning tasks.
